# Workspace structure and maintenance

## Source and generated files

`source/` holds supplied reference material. `proposal/specs/` holds the current house/site specifications; `proposal/interiors/` holds accepted room assets. Earlier stage evidence and its study scripts live in `proposal/studies/`. `scripts/` contains packages grouped by responsibility, documented in its README. Imports, shared execution module lists and build fingerprints use these package paths.

`outputs/` groups every former root `output` or `output-*` folder. Basenames are preserved to identify each generation:

| Design | Native model |
|---|---|
| Existing house | `outputs/output-walkthrough/Ashley Heights.blend` |
| Proposed (full design) | `outputs/output-proposed-compact/Ashley Heights — Proposed (compact).blend` |
| Proposed (planning application) | `outputs/output-proposed-planning/Ashley Heights — Proposed (planning application).blend` |
| Additional options | `outputs/output-redesign-{i1,i2,i3,e1,e2,e3,g1}/` |

The historical name `compact` identifies the current full Proposed design. Do not rename it independently of the variant routing. Older `output-proposed`, `output-final`, `output-reviewed`, `output-refined` and `output-scaled` generations remain retained; they are not the current full Proposed model.

The browser reads `walkthrough/public/`; `walkthrough/dist/` is regenerated by its web build. A targeted native/web update does not necessarily regenerate every standalone export. In particular, recent accepted table and basket integrations updated native models and browser assets; do not assume all standalone GLB/SketchUp/drawing exports have identical freshness. Use the existing publication/build checks for an intended release.

## Walkthrough visual quality

`make build-visuals` runs `scripts/build/regenerate_visual_quality.py` for both current proposals. Blender reads the current native models, refines coarse cushions, duvets and manufactured edges, and saves editable derivatives in `outputs/output-visual-realism-{compact,planning}/`. Input model SHA-256 checks verify that the source files were not overwritten. Browser overlays replace matching object names and preserve existing navigation.

Cycles measures six diffuse directions per probe at 192 samples. Room-local filtering suppresses samples inside furniture and fixture spikes; neutral conditioning, a small fill floor and room exposure prevent dark blotches and orange spill. The bake is an approximation of broad indirect lighting, with porous proxies for the browser's foliage. Fine contact shadows and direct sun remain live. Doors can change direct shadows, but their diffuse bounce is static until rebaked. Rebuild after geometry, layout or lighting changes; `make build-web` rejects mismatched base-model, navigation or daylight-settings hashes.

`walkthrough/public/visual-quality/daylight-settings.json` is the shared sun, sky, exposure and fixture configuration. The sunny-day bake restores and increases the actual fixture lighting (199 lights in Compact, 174 in Planning); direct sun is excluded from the diffuse bake and remains live. The visible sky uses a separate higher-resolution cubemap with the sun disc enabled. Reflection captures use the same sky direction without the tiny disc, avoiding bright reflection speckles. Changes to the shared settings require `make build-visuals` before the web build.

The accepted principal suite was imported as meshes only, leaving its downlights, bedside lamps, headboard strip, mirror lights and wardrobe strips without emitters. `scripts/interiors/principal_fixture_lighting.py` restores 33 area emitters at those existing fittings in each visual derivative (232 total lights in Compact, 207 in Planning). The Cycles bake now includes their direct illumination and bounce, including upward light on the ceiling. The original accepted asset and native source models remain unchanged. Regression checks cover measured illumination and exposure in the bedroom, dressing room and bathroom. Measurements, the before view and the browser-review limitation are recorded in `walkthrough/test-results/interior-daylight-2026-10-15/review.json` and its adjacent files.

Detailed vehicle assets live in `source/assets/vehicles/` (untouched downloads, source metadata and attribution) and `walkthrough/public/vehicles/` (browser derivatives and visible credits). Run `scripts/exports/prepare_vehicle_assets.py` through Blender to prepare the Tesla Model 3, modern Fiat 500 Abarth and Nissan NV200 panel van. Editable derivatives are in `outputs/output-vehicle-assets/`. The NV200's archived meshopt/Basis source can be decoded with `node walkthrough/tools/decode-vehicle-source.mjs source/assets/vehicles/nissan-nv200-original.glb source/assets/vehicles/nissan-nv200-decoded.glb`. Only the detailed LOD is retained; overlapping alternate LODs and taxi advertisements are removed. Tesla retains its source geometry and texture maps. Fiat retains its bodywork and texture maps, while dense tyre/brake geometry is simplified for the browser; its editable derivative retains full detail. `make build-web` applies verified lossless packing to each vehicle.

`vehicle-specs.js` defines the actual dimensions and conservative turning radii used by both route planning and collision boxes. Both proposals contain exactly one Tesla in N1, one Fiat in N2 and one van inside the garage in G1. The other parking bays stay empty, with their old vehicle meshes and collision boxes removed from the viewer. The “Driveway · vehicles” room shortcut opens a dedicated inspection position; “New double garage” shows the van. Published source navigation stays untouched; occupancy, dimensions and revised routes are applied to the generated viewer data. Routes are planned only for occupied outside bays. A car stays parked when the planner cannot establish a clear arrival and departure at its real dimensions. This is a conservative animation check, not a certified swept-path assessment.

Assets live in `walkthrough/public/visual-quality/`. The full walkthrough and isolated room previews share materials, daylight and reflections. Room reflections use a four-room cache at 256 px (64 px on touch devices). Flat glass uses Fresnel-weighted transparency so the entire house does not need a second render per frame. Screen-space contact shadows are restrained on desktop and omitted on touch devices. Natural, wide and close-detail lenses and the H/Esc presentation controls are available in the full walkthrough.

`scripts/interiors/architectural_details.py` adds construction details to the visual derivatives: three working hinges and latch faceplates on twelve previously bare solid doors, a 4 mm centre joint and recessed seals on the entrance pair, entrance jambs and thresholds, and fitted principal-suite jamb/head linings and stops. Leaf edges have small bevels. Suite undercuts account for the existing floor finishes and entrance rug. Exported `door_id` and `door_hinge` extras attach moving hardware to its leaf and place its pivot on the barrel; fixed plates and frames remain static. The source navigation and native models are preserved. Room previews include details only when their `detail_source` leaf belongs to that room.

This derivative also moves the misplaced Bedroom 4 basin emitter from floor level to its authored mirror-light position. The source builder now flushes pending transforms before moving the vanity, preventing recurrence. Rebuild both the visual assets and daylight after these changes. The web build checks the furnishings GLB hash as well as the base model, navigation and daylight settings. Evidence and regression logs live in `walkthrough/test-results/construction-details-2026-10-15/`; source and previous visual-asset copies are retained in `revisions/construction-details-2026-10-15/original/`. These details improve construction fidelity and remain active after the photographic-pass rollback.

The photographic-material and principal-suite surface-atlas experiment was withdrawn after the owner reported degraded textures and dark ceilings. A live Chrome screenshot confirmed severe mottling and a black bedroom ceiling despite a clean Cycles reference. The full walkthrough and room previews now use the original authored textures and the preceding directional daylight caches. The vehicle, door/hardware and restored fixture improvements remain active. `make build-visuals` rebuilds furnishings and directional daylight with the original materials; it does not re-enable the withdrawn pass.

The rejected implementation, texture derivatives, surface atlases and experimental checks are preserved in `revisions/oak-restoration-2026-10-15/withdrawn-photographic-pass/`. The initial state before rollback is additionally retained in `revisions/oak-restoration-2026-10-15/original/`. Original Poly Haven downloads remain in `source/assets/materials/polyhaven/`; native photographic derivatives remain in `outputs/output-visual-realism-{compact,planning}/` as experimental outputs. These are not the active browser assets. The atlas mapping and two-sided ceiling lighting were not established as correct; an explicit bake-UV change was investigated but not validated or released. Do not treat a clean native render as verification of the live viewer. Any future surface-lighting pass needs actual browser screenshots covering ceilings, curtains, bedding and oak before acceptance.

Rollback build and review evidence is in `walkthrough/test-results/oak-restoration-2026-10-15/`. Earlier photographic-pass evidence remains unchanged in `walkthrough/test-results/photographic-materials-2026-10-15/`; its final browser review was incomplete. Use `scripts/audits/audit_visual_quality.py --output <new-evidence-path>` to preserve earlier audits.

Review evidence and test logs are in `walkthrough/test-results/visual-realism-2026-10-15/`; pre-change viewer source copies are in `revisions/visual-realism-2026-10-15/original/`. Add `&diagnostics` to a local viewer URL for console timing and asset information after a short warm-up. Timing reflects the current browser, viewport and machine load, not a guaranteed device frame rate.

## Commands and entry points

From the workspace root:

```sh
make help
make build-web
make preview
make review
make check-layout
make test-python
make test-web
.venv/bin/python scripts/build/regenerate_design_outputs.py --help
.venv/bin/python scripts/build/regenerate_redesign_review.py --help
```

Blender-dependent scripts must run through Blender, not the regular Python interpreter. `scripts/build/build_extension_proposal.py` is the proposal builder; `scripts/build/build_support.py` defines dependencies and incremental freshness. See [script families](../scripts/README.md).

Finder launchers moved to `launchers/` and calculate the workspace as their parent directory. Native and application launchers remain separate from build/publish commands. Workspace timing logs go in `logs/`; individual model logs remain beside the corresponding build in `outputs/`. Local web server logs remain in `walkthrough/logs/`.

## Reviews and history

The active 100-proposal board is `revisions/whole-house-review-2026-09-29/`. Saved decisions are in its `decisions/decisions.json`; never treat them as disposable build output. Studies and accepted-integration backups remain in their dated revision folders. `archive/photo-review/` preserves older reconstruction/photo evidence and is still used by historical verification tools.

Historical reports and recorded hashes retain their original path strings as provenance. The migration manifest maps former root output paths to their new locations. Source staging translates legacy input paths when reading older build reports, without editing those reports or pretending they came from a new build. Source changes intentionally invalidate old build caches.

## Git and publication

The actual publishing repository is `deployment/ashley-heights-tour`. The workspace itself has no `.git`; the parent GitHub directory belongs to another repository. Check `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` before any Git action.

`scripts/publication/stage_redesign_sources.py` stages an authored source snapshot into the publishing checkout; it does not make this workspace an independent checkout. `scripts/publication/stage_github_pages.py` and publication scripts mutate publishing assets. Do not run them as a cleanup or local-preview step. The existing untracked `deployment/ashley-heights-tour/model 2/` was left untouched.

## Layout rules

- New full model outputs go under `outputs/`; new dated experiments and owner evidence go under `revisions/`.
- Keep generated caches under `.cache/`, temporary work under `tmp/`, and top-level run logs under `logs/`.
- Add Finder commands only to `launchers/`; document common entry points in the root README.
- Preserve accepted assets, native originals, review decisions and recovery copies. Do not infer that a large or old file can be deleted.
- Update path consumers and run the relevant checks whenever moving files. Do not add symlinks to conceal stale paths.
- Put Python implementation in the appropriate `scripts/` package. Use canonical `scripts.<package>.<module>` imports. Shared Blender execution modules retain their explicit ordered module inventory in `scripts/build/build_support.py`.

## September 2026 migration

`maintenance/restructure-manifest.json` records the initial moves and text edit hashes. Original edited text files are backed up under `.cache/restructure-backup/2026-09-29/files/`; follow-up repairs have separate backups under `followup/`. `restructure-followup.json` lists repaired consumers. `restructure_workspace.py` is a one-time migration record, **not a command to rerun**.

No design files or saved decisions were deleted. No publication was performed. Use the move manifest and backups for a deliberate rollback; do not rerun the migration or overwrite subsequent design work.

## Consistent subfolder structure

The second cleanup groups 347 implementation files by responsibility and stage evidence under `proposal/studies/`. Generated browser test output is in `walkthrough/test-results/`; executable tests and HTML fixtures remain in `walkthrough/tests/`. Current specs moved to `proposal/specs/`. Identical inspiration references now resolve to `proposal/reference/`, with original duplicate copies retained in the archive.

`maintenance/path-map.json` records old-to-current locations. Source staging resolves old report paths through this mapping without modifying historic evidence or claiming a new build. Saved owner hashes are unchanged: only source-file locations in the review inventory were updated. The review server now reloads changed inventory on each request and resolves historical source links through the move map. A server process started before this fix needs one restart using `launchers/Restart improvement review.command`; refresh existing browser tabs afterwards.

Backups for this phase are in `.cache/restructure-backup/2026-09-29-phase2`, `-phase3`, `-phase3-followup` and `-phase4`. Phase manifests are `maintenance/structure-*.json`.

## Native verification and local runtime recovery

`launchers/Verify native models.command` starts a separate background Blender process, reads the three current native models without saving them, verifies external asset paths and confirms their hashes are unchanged. Results go to `logs/native-model-verification.json`. This check has not yet completed in the restricted agent session: factory-startup Blender crashes during Metal capability detection before Python runs, while the owner reports that opening Blender normally works. The source of that launch-context difference is not yet confirmed.

The review restart launcher checks the server identity against this workspace before stopping its listener. Saved decisions remain on disk. Local socket operations are denied in the current agent sandbox, so runtime restart must happen in a session permitted to host the server.

## Open basement lounge and construction details — 16 October 2026

The first 16 October visual pass furnished the whole basement as an open social room. It misinterpreted the owner's request by replacing the bar-height island and stools with a round table. This arrangement is superseded by the wine-bar restoration below. The pass added two olive club chairs, stone side tables, a low books/drinks console, artwork, lamps, glassware and accessories. Drinks storage remained against the back wall. Pool, darts and the existing media seating remained. The initial enclosed interpretation is retained only under `revisions/interior-detail-pass-2026-10-16/withdrawn-service-bar/`.

That superseded layout was authored in the editable visual-native derivatives and their furnishings manifests. Accepted source natives, base GLBs and navigation files remained intact. Its viewer and room studies removed the 57 retired objects through `barDetails.removedObjects`; `navigationExtras` replaced the four retired collisions with ten new furniture footprints and added the back-wall mirror. The current restoration below replaces those removal rules. The active room-study page and `scripts/drawings/plan_bar_lounge.py` describe and draw the same manifest; the September plan remains historical.

`door_frame_details.py` fits static jamb/head linings, architraves on both wall faces and planted stops to every solid hinged door: 37 leaves in 33 openings for compact, 36 in 32 openings for planning. Paired doors have moving edge lippings/rebates where needed, retaining a 4 mm centre joint. Hinges, screws and latch details follow their leaves; frames and stops remain fixed. Geometry tests verify closed-leaf clearances, stop overlap and coverage. `joinery_textile_details.py` divides the 22 oak floors into 1,574 staggered boards with small bevelled joints while preserving their original texture images and UV scale, and adds cushion piping. The withdrawn photographic materials and surface atlases remain disabled.

The browser overlay installer now distinguishes authored assemblies from multi-material GLTF objects and matches full-scene objects by unique authored names. This prevents duplicate floor surfaces and missed cushion replacements. Vegetation with custom clipping is excluded from the contact-shadow depth override, removing foliage-shaped ceiling patches found in live screenshots. Bedroom lighting remains brighter; bathroom downlights are moderated separately. Bottle colours remain visible and leather does not receive the woven-fabric treatment.

Regenerate with `make build-visuals`, then `.venv/bin/python scripts/build/build_leisure_review.py` and `make build-web`. Source and asset backups are under `revisions/interior-detail-pass-2026-10-16/original/`; audit, tests and live browser-review notes are under `walkthrough/test-results/interior-detail-pass-2026-10-16/`. Live screenshots verified the open room in both proposals, added lounge furniture, closed entrance centre joint and bright bedroom ceiling. This is improved construction and furnishing fidelity, not a claim of photorealism. Nothing was published.
